title: 航空システム専門実験・演習B
subtitle: Aeronautics Major Lab/Exercises B
educationalGoal: Students will: (1)learn the method and theory of a selected basic subject, and perform experiment and practice on selected subject. (2)acquire deeper understanding and ability to apply engineering subjects. (3)learn how to write the experimental method in an experiment report. (4)learn how to create presentations on experiments and their results.
advice: Students will carry out the following experiments in Exercise B. Details on the experiments can be confirmed in the textbook. ① Wind tunnel test ② Jet engine performance test ③ Simulated flight test Students attending the lecture will be divided into three groups (A, B, and C). Group A will carry out experiment ① for five weeks and then theme ② for the next five weeks and finally theme ③ for another five weeks. Group B will follow the order of ②→③→① and group C the order of ③→①→②. In addition, class details are distributed at the time of the start of each experiment theme.
books: Textbooks: Aeronautics Major Experiments and Exercises AB Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Student should read the textbook before an experiment and understand what kind of experiment they will be carrying out. In addition, students should make a lesson report before a class as preparation, if necessary for that class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to plan an experiment and carry it out independently based on knowledge learned.
Be able to carry out tests safely based on an understanding of the principle of an experiment and the measuremen
Be able to arrange test data using computers and explain the key and problem appropriately.
Be able to reliably interpret the results of an experiment and evaluate the validity of the test data.
Be able to explain the obtained test data reasonably by comparing it with an analytical solution.
Be able to summarize the experimental results in a report, submit it before a deadline, and explain them.

achievementLevels.ideal: ① i) Explain the cylinder pressure distribution from the flow. ii) Explain the drag errors caused by measurement methods. iii) Explain precisely the forces and moment acting on the wing, and the difference between theory and experiment. ② Students properly explain engine operation principal, basic structures, operation characteristics and engine performance relating to the operation performance. ③Able to consider necessary and sufficient flight test plan considering flight safety and create a flight test sheet. Able to perform flight tests accurately.
achievementLevels.standard: ① i) Explain the cylinder pressure distribution. ii) Explain cylinder drag. iii) Explain the forces and moment acting on the wing. ②Students can understand engine operation principal and properly record performance test data. Students also understand and explain the trend of engine performance based on the operation characteristic. ③A flight test plan considering flight safety can be considered and a flight test sheet can be created.

lessons.content: Students understand the learning objectives, outline, and target abilities of this course based on the distributed syllabus. In particular, students understand which role this course assumes within the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and a rough concrete level of achievement. ① Wind tunnel test Explanation of experimental equipment and measuring device. Confirmation of prior knowledge. Verification of wind velocity. Measurement of pressure distribution on cylinder surface. Estimation of cylinder drag. Flow visualization around cylinder.
lessons.assignments: Students understand the relationship between the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and this course. ①Prepare for pressure distributions on cylinder surface. Prepare for numerical integration.

lessons.content: Measurements of wake velocity of cylinder Estimation of cylinder drag by momentum method Direct measurements of cylinder drag
Joukowsky transform Calculation of wind velocity and pressure distribution of Joukowsky airfoil Estimation of the lift acting on airfoil
Measurements of forces and moment acting on airfoil Drawing lift and drag and moment curves Drawing polar curves
lessons.assignments: Prepare for lift and drag acting on the wing

lessons.content: Presentation and discussion Students self-check the content of the experiments, reports, presentation and attendance.
lessons.assignments: Prepare for presentation by studying literature forquestion and answer session.

lessons.content: ②Students will learn the basic structure of the aeroengine, operation principal and performance measurement system. Review of the engine basic structure using cut model engine and measurement of principal dimensions. Review of the engine performance test, measurement items and measurement methods.
lessons.assignments: Preparation and review of gas turbine cycle T-S diagrams and process diagrams.
